concepts.def: A hydrocarbon with a double carbon-carbon bond. It contains carbon and hydrogen only; the C=C is what separates it from an alkane.
CₙH₂ₙ. Every member has twice as many hydrogen atoms as carbon atoms: C₂H₄, C₃H₆, C₄H₈, C₅H₁₀. The alkanes, by contrast, are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
Describes a molecule with a carbon-carbon double bond. An alkene is unsaturated because it contains two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.
Describes a molecule in which every carbon-carbon bond is single, so each carbon atom is joined to as many atoms as it can be. The alkanes are saturated.
Ethene (C₂H₄), propene (C₃H₆), butene (C₄H₈) and pentene (C₅H₁₀). The series begins at two carbon atoms because a C=C needs two carbon atoms.
A formula such as C₃H₆ that gives the number of atoms of each element in one molecule. It does not show how the atoms are joined or where the double bond lies.
A drawing showing every atom and every bond in the molecule, so a C=C appears as two lines between two carbon atoms. It carries more information than a molecular formula.
The group of atoms in a molecule that gives a homologous series its characteristic reactions. Members of a series share a functional group and so react in the same ways.
The carbon-carbon double bond, the functional group of the alkenes. It is the site of their addition reactions.
It is the generality of reactions of functional groups that determines the reactions of organic compounds, so ethene, propene, butene and pentene all react in the same ways.
Alkenes react with oxygen in combustion reactions like other hydrocarbons, but tend to burn in air with smoky flames because combustion is incomplete and carbon is released as soot.
A reaction in which atoms add across the carbon-carbon double bond so that the double bond becomes a single carbon-carbon bond. Alkenes react in this way with hydrogen, water and the halogens.
Hydrogen adds across the C=C over a nickel catalyst at about 150 °C, turning the alkene into the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms: ethene gives ethane.
Ethene reacts with steam in the presence of a catalyst, at high temperature and pressure, and water adds across the double bond to give an alcohol: ethene gives ethanol.
Chlorine, bromine or iodine adds across the C=C at room temperature. Bromine water is decolourised, which is the test that tells an alkene from an alkane.
A compound containing the functional group –OH. Alcohols are not hydrocarbons, because they contain oxygen as well as carbon and hydrogen.
Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol, the first four members of a homologous series of alcohols.
Ethanol may be written as CH₃CH₂OH, which shows the –OH group and how the carbon atoms are grouped, or drawn as a displayed formula showing every bond.
Sodium reacts with an alcohol, fizzing steadily and releasing hydrogen gas. The reaction is gentler than that of sodium with water.
Alcohols burn in air. Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water, for example C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.
The first four alcohols dissolve in water, and the solutions formed have a neutral pH.
Warming an alcohol with an oxidising agent produces the carboxylic acid with the same number of carbon atoms: ethanol gives ethanoic acid.
The first four alcohols are used as fuels and as solvents; ethanol is also the alcohol in alcoholic drinks.
The process in which aqueous solutions of ethanol are produced when sugar solutions are fermented using yeast.
Yeast is added to an aqueous sugar solution kept warm at about 30 °C with air kept out. Too high a temperature kills the yeast and stops the process.
An alcohol can be picked out from a name ending in -ol, such as butanol, or from a formula containing the –OH group, such as CH₃CH₂OH.
A compound containing the functional group –COOH. Its aqueous solutions are acidic.
Methanoic acid, ethanoic acid, propanoic acid and butanoic acid, the first four members of a homologous series of carboxylic acids.
Ethanoic acid may be written as CH₃COOH, which shows the carboxyl group joined to a CH₃ group, or drawn as a displayed formula showing every bond.
The drawing shows the C=O and the O–H of the carboxyl group as separate bonds, which CH₃COOH written on one line does not set out.
A carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate, fizzing as carbon dioxide is given off, in the same way as other acids do.
Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to give acidic solutions with a pH below 7.
A carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol, in the presence of an acid catalyst, to produce an ester. Ethanoic acid with ethanol gives ethyl ethanoate.
An acid that is only partially ionised in aqueous solution. The carboxylic acids are weak acids.
Because only some molecules ionise, a weak acid solution has a lower concentration of H+ ions, and so a higher pH, than a strong acid of the same concentration.
A carboxylic acid can be picked out from a name ending in -oic acid, such as propanoic acid, or from a formula containing –COOH, such as CH₃COOH.

mcqs.q: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkenes?
options: CₙH₂ₙ — twice as many hydrogen atoms as carbon atoms
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — two hydrogen atoms more than twice the carbon
CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ — two hydrogen atoms fewer than twice the carbons
CₙHₙ — one hydrogen atom for every carbon atom present
mcqs.explain: The specification gives CₙH₂ₙ for the alkenes: propene is C₃H₆ and butene is C₄H₈.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a correct description of an alkene?
options: A hydrocarbon in which every carbon bond is a single bond
A hydrocarbon containing a carbon–carbon double bond
A compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms
A hydrocarbon made unreactive by its double bond
mcqs.explain: Alkenes are hydrocarbons with a double carbon-carbon bond, as the specification states.

mcqs.q: Propane has the formula C₃H₈. What is the formula of propene?
options: C₃H₁₀, which is two hydrogen atoms more than propane
C₃H₆, two hydrogen atoms fewer than propane
C₃H₈, exactly the same formula as propane has
C₃H₇, one hydrogen atom fewer than propane has
mcqs.explain: An alkene has two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.

mcqs.q: Why is propene described as unsaturated?
options: It has two hydrogen atoms fewer than propane does
It has two hydrogen atoms more than propane does
Every bond between its carbon atoms is a single bond
Each carbon atom is joined to as many atoms as it can be
mcqs.explain: The specification defines unsaturated in exactly this way: two fewer hydrogen atoms than the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of alkenes?
options: Methene, ethene, propene and pentene
Ethene, ethane, butene and butane
Ethene, propene, butene and pentene
Ethene, propene, butene and hexene
mcqs.explain: These are the four members named in the specification.

mcqs.q: What does the molecular formula C₃H₆ tell you about a propene molecule?
options: The number of atoms of each element in the molecule
Where the double bond lies and how the atoms join
Only the ratio of carbon to hydrogen atoms present
Every bond in the molecule, shown drawn out
mcqs.explain: A molecular formula gives the actual count of each kind of atom: three carbon and six hydrogen.

mcqs.q: Which of these formulae fits the general formula CₙH₂ₙ?
options: C₄H₁₀
C₂H₅OH
CH₃COOH
C₃H₆
mcqs.explain: Six hydrogen atoms for three carbon atoms is 2n hydrogen atoms, so this fits the alkenes.

mcqs.q: Propene can also be drawn as a fully displayed formula. What does that show that C₃H₆ does not?
options: Nothing new; the same information is drawn out
Only how many atoms of each element are present
Every atom and every bond, including the double bond
How the molecules are arranged in a sample of propene
mcqs.explain: A displayed formula sets out each bond, so the position of the C=C can be seen.

mcqs.q: What is the functional group of the alkenes?
options: The –OH group found in alcohols
The –COOH group of the acids
The carbon–carbon double bond, C=C
A single carbon–carbon bond, C–C
mcqs.explain: The specification gives the functional group of the alkenes as C=C.

mcqs.q: Ethene, propene and butene all decolourise bromine water. What best explains this?
options: They share a functional group, so they react alike
Each one has its own reaction and the likeness is chance
They all contain the same number of carbon atoms
They are all gases, so they mix easily with bromine
mcqs.explain: It is the generality of reactions of functional groups that determines the reactions of organic compounds.

mcqs.q: How do alkenes tend to burn in air?
options: With clean blue flames, because combustion is complete
They do not burn at all, as the double bond is stable
With smoky flames, because combustion is incomplete
With smoky flames, because the oxygen supply is too great
mcqs.explain: The specification states that alkenes tend to burn in air with smoky flames because of incomplete combustion.

mcqs.q: Ethene is burned in plenty of air. What are the products of complete combustion?
options: Carbon dioxide and soot
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Carbon monoxide and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and water
mcqs.explain: Alkenes react with oxygen in combustion reactions in the same way as other hydrocarbons.

mcqs.q: Hydrogen adds to ethene. What happens to the carbon–carbon double bond?
options: It stays a double bond in the product
It breaks and the molecule splits into two
It is swapped for a bond to a hydrogen atom
It becomes a single carbon–carbon bond
mcqs.explain: In addition reactions atoms add across the double bond so that it becomes a single carbon-carbon bond.

mcqs.q: Which set of substances react with alkenes by addition across the double bond?
options: Hydrogen, water and the halogens
Oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Oxygen, sodium and the halogens
Sodium, oxygen and carbonates
mcqs.explain: The specification lists hydrogen, water and the halogens as adding across the carbon-carbon double bond.

mcqs.q: What conditions are used for the addition of hydrogen to an alkene?
options: Ultraviolet light, no catalyst
Steam with a catalyst at 300 °C
Yeast at about 30 °C with no air
A nickel catalyst at about 150 °C
mcqs.explain: Hydrogenation of an alkene is carried out over a nickel catalyst at roughly 150 °C.

mcqs.q: Ethene is reacted with steam in the presence of a catalyst. What is produced?
options: Ethane gas, an alkane, C₂H₆
Ethanol, an alcohol, CH₃CH₂OH
Ethanoic acid, an acid, CH₃COOH
A solution of ethene in hot water
mcqs.explain: Water adds across the double bond, so the product of hydrating ethene is ethanol.

mcqs.q: Bromine water is shaken with ethene. What is seen, and what is formed?
options: The orange colour goes as C₂H₃Br and HBr form
The orange colour stays, as ethene is saturated
The orange colour deepens as bromine adds on
The orange colour goes and C₂H₄Br₂ forms
mcqs.explain: Bromine adds across the double bond, so the bromine colour is lost and a dibromo compound forms.

mcqs.q: Ethene reacts with chlorine. Which describes the product?
options: C₂H₃Cl, with a hydrogen atom replaced by chlorine
C₂H₄ and Cl₂ are unchanged, as there is no reaction
C₂H₄Cl₂, one chlorine atom on each carbon atom
C₂H₄Cl₂, still holding a carbon–carbon double bond
mcqs.explain: Both chlorine atoms add across the double bond, giving a saturated molecule with two chlorine atoms.

mcqs.q: Propene reacts with hydrogen. How many hydrogen atoms are in the displayed formula of the product?
options: Six, as propene already has six of them
Seven, one hydrogen atom having added on
Eight, since the product is propane, C₃H₈
Ten, since two molecules of H₂ add on
mcqs.explain: Two hydrogen atoms add across the double bond of C₃H₆, giving C₃H₈.

mcqs.q: Which functional group is found in every alcohol?
options: The carboxyl group, –COOH
The hydroxyl group, –OH
A carbon–carbon double bond
The hydroxide ion, OH⁻
mcqs.explain: The specification states that alcohols contain the functional group -OH.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of alcohols?
options: Methanol, ethanol, propanol and pentanol
Ethanol, propanol, butanol, pentanol
Methane, ethanol, propanol and butanol
Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol
mcqs.explain: These are the four alcohols named in the specification.

mcqs.q: Ethanol can be represented as CH₃CH₂OH. What does this form show?
options: Only the total number of atoms of each element
The –OH group and how the carbon atoms are grouped
Every bond in the molecule, drawn in full
That ethanol releases hydroxide ions in water
mcqs.explain: This form sets out the groups in the molecule, so the functional group can be picked out.

mcqs.q: A displayed formula of ethanol is drawn instead of writing CH₃CH₂OH. What does the drawing add?
options: It shows nothing new about the ethanol molecule
It shows every bond, including the O–H bond
It shows how many molecules are in the sample
It shows the charge on each atom present
mcqs.explain: A displayed formula shows all of the bonds in the molecule, which the written form does not.

mcqs.q: A small piece of sodium is added to ethanol. What is observed?
options: It fizzes steadily and hydrogen gas is given off
It fizzes gently and oxygen is given off
Nothing happens; sodium reacts only with water
It fizzes and carbon dioxide gas is released
mcqs.explain: Alcohols react with sodium to give off hydrogen, more gently than water does.

mcqs.q: Ethanol burns completely in air. What are the products?
options: Carbon monoxide and water
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and water
Ethanoic acid and steam
mcqs.explain: Complete combustion of an alcohol gives carbon dioxide and water.

mcqs.q: Which equation correctly represents the complete combustion of ethanol?
options: C₂H₅OH + 2O₂ → 2CO₂ + H₂O
C₂H₅OH + O₂ → 2CO₂ + H₂O
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O
C₂H₅OH + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
mcqs.explain: Balanced: two carbon atoms, six hydrogen atoms and seven oxygen atoms on each side.

mcqs.q: What happens when ethanol is added to water?
options: It dissolves and the solution has a pH below 7
It floats as a layer and does not mix at all
It dissolves fully, giving a neutral solution
It reacts and hydrogen gas is given off
mcqs.explain: The first four alcohols dissolve in water and their solutions have a neutral pH.

mcqs.q: Ethanol is warmed with an oxidising agent. What is formed?
options: Ethene, formed by the loss of a water molecule
Carbon dioxide and water, as when it burns
Ethanoic acid, which is a carboxylic acid
Ethyl ethanoate, an ester of the alcohol
mcqs.explain: Oxidation of an alcohol produces the carboxylic acid with the same number of carbon atoms.

mcqs.q: Which statement gives main uses of the first four alcohols?
options: They are used as fuels and as solvents
They are used only for alcoholic drinks
They are used as fuels but never as solvents
They are used mainly to neutralise acids
mcqs.explain: The specification requires recall of the main uses of these alcohols: as fuels and as solvents.

mcqs.q: How are aqueous solutions of ethanol produced from sugar?
options: The sugar solution is fermented using yeast
The sugar solution is distilled with a catalyst
The sugar is reacted with steam and a catalyst
The sugar solution is warmed with an acid
mcqs.explain: The specification states that aqueous solutions of ethanol are produced when sugar solutions are fermented using yeast.

mcqs.q: Which conditions are used for the fermentation of sugar using yeast?
options: About 100 °C, in solution, with air kept out
About 30 °C, in solution, with air kept out
About 30 °C, in solution, with air bubbled in
About 300 °C and high pressure, with a catalyst
mcqs.explain: Fermentation needs yeast, an aqueous sugar solution, a warm temperature of roughly 30 °C and anaerobic conditions.

mcqs.q: Which of these formulae is that of an alcohol?
options: CH₃COOH
C₃H₆
CH₃COOCH₂CH₃
CH₃CH₂OH
mcqs.explain: The –OH functional group at the end of the chain makes this an alcohol, ethanol.

mcqs.q: Which functional group do carboxylic acids contain?
options: The carboxyl group, –COOH
The hydroxyl group, –OH
A carbon–carbon double bond
The ester group, –COO–
mcqs.explain: The specification gives the functional group of the carboxylic acids as -COOH.

mcqs.q: Which list gives the first four members of the homologous series of carboxylic acids?
options: Ethanoic, propanoic, butanoic, pentanoic acid
Methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic and butanoic acid
Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol
Methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic, pentanoic acid
mcqs.explain: These are the four carboxylic acids named in the specification.

mcqs.q: Ethanoic acid can be represented as CH₃COOH. What does this form show?
options: An –OH group on a chain of two carbons
A –COOH group joined to a CH₃ group
Every bond of the acid, drawn out
Just the atom count, like C₂H₄O₂
mcqs.explain: Writing it this way separates the carboxyl group from the rest of the molecule.

mcqs.q: Ethanoic acid is added to sodium carbonate. What happens?
options: It fizzes gently and hydrogen gas is given off
There is no reaction, since it is only a weak acid
A white precipitate forms and the mixture clouds
It fizzes and carbon dioxide gas is given off
mcqs.explain: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to release carbon dioxide, as other acids do.

mcqs.q: What happens when ethanoic acid dissolves in water?
options: An acidic solution forms, with a pH below 7
A neutral solution forms, as with ethanol
It does not dissolve, being an organic liquid
An alkaline solution forms, from the –OH
mcqs.explain: Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to give acidic solutions.

mcqs.q: Ethanoic acid is warmed with ethanol and an acid catalyst. What is formed?
options: Ethyl ethanoate, an ester, together with water
A salt and water only, as in neutralisation
Carbon dioxide and water, as with a carbonate
Sodium ethanoate and some hydrogen gas
mcqs.explain: A carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol to produce an ester; here the ester is ethyl ethanoate.

mcqs.q: Why is ethanoic acid described as a weak acid?
options: All of its molecules ionise in aqueous solution
Only some of its molecules ionise in solution
Its solutions are dilute rather than concentrated
It holds fewer hydrogen atoms than a strong acid
mcqs.explain: A weak acid is only partially ionised in aqueous solution.

mcqs.q: Solutions of hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid have the same concentration. How do their pH values compare?
options: Ethanoic acid has the lower pH of the two
Both have the same pH, as both are acids
Ethanoic acid has a pH of more than 7
Ethanoic acid has the higher pH of the two
mcqs.explain: It ionises only partially, so its solution has a lower concentration of H+ ions and a higher pH.

mcqs.q: Which of these formulae is that of a carboxylic acid?
options: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
CH₃CH₂OH
C₃H₆
CH₃CH₂COOH
mcqs.explain: The –COOH group at the end of the chain makes this propanoic acid.

specSource: AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) specification; section 4.7.2 Reactions of alkenes and alcohols (chemistry only)
